neighbours.label: The auxiliary in an inverted 'so do', 'as did', 'as does', 'so is'; ordinary do, did and is stay quiet
fire: As prices rise, so do wages in the city.
The flood damaged the school, as did a later storm.
Painters have settled here, as does a poet each summer.
The birds sing, and so do the children.
Rents are higher here, and so is the cost of food.
My sister loves opera, as did our late mother.
As the days grow longer, so does the grass.
The village lost power, as did three nearby towns.
quiet: What do wages look like in the city?
The flood did not damage the school at all.
Painters do not settle here, and a poet does not visit.
The birds did sing, but the children did not.
Rents are higher here, and the food is good.
My sister does not love opera, and neither did I.
What does the grass need in longer days?
The village did lose power in the storm.
